title: Word Order and Emphasis
summary: Use fronting, cleft sentences, topicalization, and adverb placement to emphasize information naturally.

sections.heading: Neutral order and flexible emphasis
sections.body: Neutral Brazilian Portuguese usually follows **subject + verb + object**, but speakers can move elements to highlight contrast or connect to previous context.

sections.heading: Cleft sentences with é que / foi que
sections.body: Cleft structures emphasize one element by framing it with **é que** or **foi que**. They are common in speech and writing, but should not be overused.

examples.pt: É disso que eu estou falando.
examples.en: That is what I am talking about.
It was yesterday that they arrived.

sections.heading: Adverb placement and scope
sections.body: Where an adverb appears can change what it modifies. Place adverbs near the word or phrase they affect, especially **só**, **também**, **ainda**, and **já**.

examples.note: I did not do anything else

keyPoints: Neutral order is subject + verb + object, but Portuguese allows fronting for emphasis.
Topicalized elements often appear at the beginning followed by a pause/comma.
É que and foi que create strong focus.
Adverb position affects meaning and scope.
Use marked word order for a reason: contrast, continuity, or emphasis.

commonMistakes.wrong: Moving words randomly to sound advanced.
commonMistakes.right: Move words only when the focus or context justifies it.
commonMistakes.note: Marked word order creates marked meaning.
Só normally comes before the phrase it limits.
The focused element goes between foi and que.
